extracted.intended_audience: inventors, in-house counsels, foreign applicants and patent practitioners seeking to file or prosecute patents in Brazil (INPI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, filing, prosecuting, and accelerating patent, utility model, and industrial design applications before Brazil's INPI, including direct filings and PCT national phase entry requirements and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Invention Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention patents are granted for products or processes that meet the requirements of novelty, inventive step, and industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions include new products (compounds, devices, machines) or processes/methods across any field of technology. Term is 20 years from the filing date. Examiner will assess novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability during substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility Model eligibility and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility models protect an object of practical use, usually a shape or structural improvement in a tool or apparatus that is industrially applicable; processes or chemical compositions cannot be utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive threshold is lower than for invention patents (often called 'petty patents'). Utility models undergo substantive examination in Brazil. Term is 15 years from filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial Design (Desenho Industrial) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design protects the ornamental visual design of an object or pattern (the aesthetic appearance); functionality is not protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple related design variations (up to 20) can be included in one application if they share the same distinctive characteristics. Design applications undergo only formal examination; if formal requirements are met, the design is granted and published without substantive novelty examination. Initial term 10 years from filing, renewable three additional 5-year periods to a maximum of 25 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required filing documents for Brazilian applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A Brazilian application requires a request form, the specifications, claims, abstract, and drawings (in Portuguese as noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming priority under the Paris Convention, a certified copy of the priority document with a simple Portuguese translation must be provided within prescribed time (commonly 90 days). If the applicant is not the inventor, an assignment or inventor’s release may be required (simple copy with translation can be filed within about 3 months). Drawings and sequence listings (if applicable) should be included at filing, as missing drawings cannot be added later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of Attorney (POA) and local agent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applicants must appoint a local Brazilian agent and maintain a local address for service; a Power of Attorney appointing a Brazilian patent agent is a key document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brazil allows a POA to be filed after the application (within 60 days), and no notarization or legalization is needed. While INPI may not require the POA at the exact filing moment, submitting it with the application (or soon after) is highly recommended to avoid a formal office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The official language for patents in Brazil is Portuguese; a Brazilian patent application must be filed in Portuguese or accompanied by a Portuguese translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum the title, abstract, and claims must be in Portuguese at filing. If the specification is initially in another language, INPI allows a short window (usually 30 days after filing) to submit the full Portuguese translation. It is recommended to have the full application in Portuguese at filing to avoid issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing and payment procedure (e-INPI / GRU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brazil uses an electronic filing system (e-INPI); applicants must create an e-INPI account and pay the filing fee via a GRU (government payment form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the fee is paid and forms completed online, the application can be submitted. The filing date is accorded once INPI receives the documents and payment. Missing required elements (like claims or drawings) may trigger a notice to correct deficiencies; failing to correct timely can lead to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly filed patent application in Brazil remains confidential for 18 months from the filing date or earliest priority date, after which INPI publishes it in the Industrial Property Gazette (RPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is automatic (applicant does not need to act) except paying the publication fee as part of filing fees. Applicants may request early publication anytime after filing to expedite public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination deadline (direct filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must file a request for examination within 36 months (3 years) from the Brazilian filing date (or from the international filing date for national phase applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to request examination in time, the application will be deemed withdrawn (shelved). INPI allows a grace period of an additional 60 days after the 36-month deadline to request examination with payment of a late fee. Many applicants strategically delay requesting examination to defer costs, but requesting earlier places the application in the examination queue sooner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination process and Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once examination is requested and the application published, an INPI examiner will review formal requirements and patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial application) and may issue Office Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common issues include clarity or breadth of claims, adequacy of disclosure, and patentability over prior art. Applicants typically have 90 days to respond to an Office Action (extendable once for 60 days upon petition). Responses may include arguments or amendments; multiple Office Actions can be issued until objections are overcome or final refusal is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance, grant fee payment, and issue
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner is satisfied, INPI will issue a Notice of Allowance (Despacho de Concessão/Deferimento).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The allowance is published in the RPI, and the applicant must pay the grant (issuance) fee within 60 days. There is a brief grace period with surcharge for late payment. Failure to pay the grant fee in time can lead to lapse of the allowance. Upon payment, INPI issues the patent certificate and publishes the grant; the patent is enforceable subject to post-grant challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees (annuities) start and payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In Brazil annuities start while the application is pending; annual fees begin accruing at the start of the 3rd year from the filing date (i.e., after 2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first annuity must be paid by the end of the month in which the application's second anniversary occurs, with a 3-month window and a 6-month grace period with surcharge. Subsequent annuities are due yearly. If an annuity is not paid the application (or patent) can be extinguished, though a 6-month grace period after each due date is provided with late fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase entry deadline (Brazil)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brazil has a 30-month deadline from the priority date to enter the national phase for PCT applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brazil does not grant routine extensions of the 30-month deadline. If the 30-month date is missed, you can petition INPI to accept a late entry within 2 months from removal of the cause of delay or up to 12 months from the 30-month deadline, whichever is earlier; the applicant must show the delay was unintentional or due care was taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase filing requirements and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter the national phase in Brazil, submit a copy of the International Application (PCT publication), Portuguese translation of the PCT application (at least specification and claims), any amendments with translations, and accompanying documents like drawings/sequence listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the time of national phase filing, Brazil requires the title, abstract, and claims in Portuguese. If the PCT specification was in another language, Brazil allows a short 60-day extension after national phase filing to submit the full Portuguese translation of the description. Filing is via e-INPI and the national phase application receives a Brazilian application number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment / applicant name rules for national phase entry
rubrics_metrics.description: If the entity entering national phase is not the same as the one named in the PCT publication as applicant, an assignment document or a simple document evidencing the transfer should be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brazil’s law allows 180 days from national filing to provide an assignment for a priority right transfer. If the PCT was filed with the correct applicant name, this is often not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination request deadline counting for PCT national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: For PCT national phase entries, examination must be requested within 36 months of the international filing date, not the date of entry in Brazil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines like examination request and annuities are counted from the international date as specified by law; failure to account for the international date can lead to missed deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annuity timing for PCT national phase entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Annuity payments for a PCT National Phase Application in Brazil start similarly to direct filings at the beginning of the third year from the international date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 24th month has passed by the time of national entry, the first annuity comes due within 3 months of entering the national phase. Future annuities follow the yearly schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination — Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brazil participates in PPH programs with several major offices; under PPH, if you have at least one allowed claim in a corresponding application in a partner jurisdiction you can request accelerated examination in Brazil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH requests must be filed after Brazilian publication and before the examination stage begins. You must show an allowed claim and map Brazil’s claims to those allowed claims. Brazil currently caps PPH requests at 800 per year and operates on a first-come basis. If granted, PPH can move the application to the front of the line and often lead to a first Office Action within months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination — Prioritized examination (exame prioritário)
rubrics_metrics.description: INPI offers prioritized examination categories based on subject matter or applicant status (exame prioritário).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories include green technologies, healthcare (including COVID-19), startups, small entities, research institutions, evidence of infringement, needs for financing/investment, applicants over 60, and applicants with certain disabilities or illnesses. Check INPI official guidance for full eligibility, required evidence, and procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and weight of international search/examination reports
rubrics_metrics.description: International Search Report (ISR) and International Preliminary Examination Report (IPER) from the PCT phase do not automatically bind INPI but examiners often consider them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A favorable IPRP or positive findings abroad can be cited and used to request PPH or otherwise argue for accelerated treatment or allowance in Brazil, but INPI retains independent examination authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic filing recommendations and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical recommendations: file early in Portuguese (or quickly provide translations), appoint local counsel, monitor INPI deadlines, and consider accelerated examination options when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delaying examination can defer costs but slows prosecution; missing procedural requirements (translations, POA, annuities, examination request) can lead to abandonment. Local counsel is essential for navigating INPI formalities and monitoring the process.
